- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting an initial overshoot bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes in price, indicating a lag in adjusting to sustained upward momentum.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical averages too quickly, missing prolonged trends.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., 2025-01-23), model overreacts to minor fluctuations, producing exaggerated upward swings.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility — model reacts to short-term noise rather than underlying trend persistence.
- Model underestimates the persistence of upward trends in the 30-day window, especially when prices are trending upward for >10 days.
- Forecasts often fail to account for seasonal or policy-driven price corrections (e.g., ETS cap adjustments) that occur mid-horizon.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — underestimates “pullback” depth and timing.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp price drops, underestimating the severity of downward corrections.
- Model exhibits a “late correction” bias — corrects too late in the forecast horizon, missing the true turning point by 3–5 days.
